1.why: Reset verification requires record.sessionId === session.id, so the token is bound to the requesting session before MFA proceeds.

2.why: The same token fails verification in another session because of the sessionId check and single-use delete after success.

3.why: Password change only updates passwordHash and clears mfaVerified; other sessions in the Map are not invalidated.

4.why: Bun serves TLS on 3000 with HSTS and HTTP redirects to HTTPS, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords with argon2id, but MFA codes and session fields sit in memory plaintext and are not encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API uses a generic recovery message, yet testingToken is returned in the JSON body for academic testing.

7.why: Contact format, token shape, and password policy are validated server-side, and the UI only uses textContent/JSON rather than raw HTML injection.

8.why: Navigation is path-only on the same origin; HTTP only 308-redirects to the local HTTPS site with no user-controlled open redirect.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user input; recovery responses are fixed strings without HTML from clients.

10.why: testingToken and testingMfaCode are returned by the API and written into the on-page Logs panel, exposing tokens.

11.why: Password hash comes from env/argon2id, but recovery and login MFA codes are hardcoded secrets in the source (482913, 741852).

12.why: No default password is embedded; login requires a non-empty passwordHash verified with Bun.password.verify.

13.why: recordAttempt/blocked enforce per-action limits (e.g. 3–5 tries) and a 60s lockout on recovery, verify, MFA, and login.

14.why: Invalid and valid recovery contacts both receive the same generic eligibility message with no existence oracle.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomHex(32) (64 hex chars), hashed at rest, short-lived, single-use, and bound to the creating session.
